answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single comet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 427 aliases thus costs 141 bonds held for 12 days each, plus the knoll attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a whisper, before it can post or attest. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
